title: Set the shelf hold for donated produce
body:
# Set the shelf hold for donated produce

## Context
Donated produce arrives in mixed condition and the pantry has one shelf for it.

## Decision
Donated produce stays on the shelf for 48 hours. Whatever is still there when the hold ends is discarded. The volunteer writes the arrival time on the crate label when produce comes in.

## Consequences
The shelf turns over often and the front table stays tidy.

title: Plan Saturday restocking around the discard window
body:
# Plan Saturday restocking around the discard window

## Context
The Saturday crew restocks the front shelf from the Friday delivery.

## Decision
Produce goes into the compost bin two days after it arrives, so the Saturday crew clears anything older before it sets out new crates.

## Consequences
The front shelf is full when the doors open.

title: Label every crate with a donor name
body:
# Label every crate with a donor name

## Context
Donors like to know their crate was used.

## Decision
The volunteer requests a name from each donor or initials and writes them on the crate label. The shelf rules in decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce apply to labelled crates like any other.

## Consequences
Thank-you notes can name the right donor.

title: Keep citrus on its own shelf
body:
# Keep citrus on its own shelf

## Context
Citrus crates are heavy and roll off the front shelf.

## Decision
Citrus goes on the low shelf by the door, in the crates it arrived in. Read decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce for everything else on the table.

## Consequences
The front shelf holds only light crates.

title: Print a sign for the produce table
body:
# Print a sign for the produce table

Print a large sign for the produce table that points volunteers to decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce, and tape it to the wall above the crates.

title: Count the crates at closing
body:
# Count the crates at closing

Count the crates left on the produce table when the doors close and write the number on the clipboard by the exit. This follows the shelf rules in decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce.

title: Buy gloves for the shelf crew
body:
# Buy gloves for the shelf crew

Buy a box of disposable gloves for the volunteers who clear the produce table, in whatever sizes the crew requests. The grounds are in decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce.

title: Ask the food bank about a second fridge
body:
# Ask the food bank about a second fridge

Ask the regional food bank whether they have a spare fridge for donated produce, and what the delivery arrangements would be. A fridge would change how decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce is used, so report back to the coordinator.

title: Unlabelled crates are slow to sort
body:
# Unlabelled crates are slow to sort

A crate with no label costs the volunteer a trip to the coordinator to learn who dropped it off. The label rule in decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce exists to prevent this, and the lesson is to refuse a crate that arrives bare.

title: Produce table
body:
# Produce table

The produce table is the first thing visitors see. It runs under decision/set-the-shelf-hold-for-donated-produce, and the coordinator checks it at the start of each shift. Volunteers keep the crates facing outward and the signs in view.
